question: For the supplied explicit cylinder encoding/decoding formulas over a commutative ring, prove decode(encode(q,w))=(q,w) when q satisfies the hypersurface equation and multiplication by q.p³ is injective.
statement:
lemma decode_encode (q : Point R) (w : R) (hq : q.equation = 0)
    (hp : ∀ r : R, q.p ^ 3 * r = 0 → r = 0) :
    decode (encode q w).1 (encode q w).2 = (q, w)
subject: Algebraic and complex geometry
title: Invert the explicit cylinder encoding

question: In the specified determinant algebra T with a*c−b*d=1 and fiber Euler operator, show that a nonzero locally nilpotent derivation E of nonpositive fiber shift cannot fix a,d,u simultaneously.
statement:
lemma fixed_coefficients_contradiction (E : Derivation ℂ T T)
    (hE : E ≠ 0) (hln : LND.LocallyNilpotent E) (e : ℤ) (he : e ≤ 0)
    (hshift : FiberShift E e) (ha : E a = 0) (hd : E d = 0) (hu : E u = 0) : False
subject: Algebraic and complex geometry
title: Nonpositive fiber shift contradicts fixed coefficients

question: In the specified determinant algebra T, prove that a locally nilpotent derivation E with nonpositive fiber Euler shift and E²(v)=0 is identically zero, where v is the source’s distinguished expression.
statement:
theorem rigidity (E : Derivation ℂ T T) (hln : LND.LocallyNilpotent E)
    (e : ℤ) (he : e ≤ 0) (hshift : FiberShift E e) (hv : E (E v) = 0) : E = 0
subject: Algebraic and complex geometry
title: Derive full determinant rigidity from a square-zero distinguished orbit

question: Given a nonzero locally nilpotent derivation D on the defined degeneration algebra G, construct a nonzero multiplier c∈G and a nonzero locally nilpotent derivation E on the bundle algebra B such that E(pullback(r))=pullback(cD(r)) and E commutes with the fiber Euler derivation.
statement:
lemma exists_equivariant_lift (D : Derivation ℂ Degeneration.G Degeneration.G)
    (hD : LND.LocallyNilpotent D) (hDn : D ≠ 0) :
    ∃ (c : Degeneration.G) (E : Derivation ℂ Bundle.B Bundle.B),
      c ≠ 0 ∧ LND.LocallyNilpotent E ∧ E ≠ 0 ∧
      (∀ r, E (Bundle.pullback r)=Bundle.pullback (c*D r)) ∧
      ∀ b, Bundle.fiberEuler (E b)=E (Bundle.fiberEuler b)
subject: Algebraic and complex geometry
title: Lift a locally nilpotent derivation equivariantly

question: For the supplied graded modification algebra T(R,v), let D be a nonzero homogeneous locally nilpotent derivation fixing V and commuting with the lifted Euler derivation associated to H(v)=2v. Construct a nonzero locally nilpotent derivation E of R and n≥0 with [H,E]=−nE and E²(v)=0, without assuming D preserves the coefficient ring.
statement:
theorem extract (H : Derivation k R R) (hH : H v=2*v)
    (D : Derivation k (T R v) (T R v)) (hD : LND.LocallyNilpotent D) (hDn : D ≠ 0)
    (j : ℤ) (hshift : ∀ e r, r ∈ pieces R v e → D r ∈ pieces R v (e+j))
    (hcomm : ∀ z, euler v H hH (D z)=D (euler v H hH z))
    (hV : D (V R v)=0) :
    ∃ (E : Derivation k R R) (n : ℕ), E ≠ 0 ∧ LND.LocallyNilpotent E ∧
      (∀ r, H (E r)-E (H r)=-(n • E r)) ∧ E (E v)=0
subject: Algebraic and complex geometry
title: Extract a coefficient-ring derivation from a modification

question: For the specified Rees algebra B and special-fiber reduction red:B→G, let E be a nonzero locally nilpotent derivation fixing the deformation parameter q and an element s. Construct a nonzero locally nilpotent derivation D on G that fixes red(s).
statement:
lemma primitive_reduction (E : Derivation ℂ B B) (hE : LND.LocallyNilpotent E)
    (hEn : E ≠ 0) (hEq : E q=0) (s : B) (hEs : E s=0) :
    ∃ D : Derivation ℂ Degeneration.G Degeneration.G,
      LND.LocallyNilpotent D ∧ D ≠ 0 ∧ D (red s)=0
subject: Algebraic and complex geometry
title: Preserve a nonzero derivation through primitive Rees specialization

question: Let k be a characteristic-zero field and a,d,u,n be nonzero polynomials with deg(n)≤1 and d²+a²u³=n. Assume −u(0)³ is not a square in k. Prove a,d,u are constant polynomials.
statement:
theorem orbit_constant [CharZero k] {a d u n : k[X]}
    (ha : a ≠ 0) (hd : d ≠ 0) (hu : u ≠ 0) (hn : n ≠ 0)
    (hdeg : n.natDegree ≤ 1) (heq : d ^ 2 + a ^ 2 * u ^ 3 = n)
    (hns : ∀ z : k, z ^ 2 ≠ -(u.coeff 0) ^ 3) :
    a = C (a.coeff 0) ∧ d = C (d.coeff 0) ∧ u = C (u.coeff 0)
subject: Algebraic and complex geometry
title: Mason–Stothers rigidity of polynomial orbits

question: For every n≥4 and the source’s specific extended polynomial F_n and localization coordinate equivalence, prove an ambient polynomial becomes a constant in the localized polynomial coordinates exactly when it lies in the original subalgebra C[F_n].
statement:
theorem extended_localization_kernel_intersection {n : ℕ} (hn : 4 ≤ n)
    (r : MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℂ) :
    (∃ b : LaurentCoefficients,
      extendedLocalizationEquiv hn (extendedLocMap hn r) = C b) ↔
    r ∈ Algebra.adjoin ℂ ({extendedF hn} : Set (MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℂ))
subject: Algebraic and complex geometry
title: Identify the actual all-dimensional localized common kernel

question: Let an injective K-algebra map A→L send c to a unit. Suppose a finite family of derivations on A is obtained from derivations D_i on L by direction-dependent powers c^(N_i), the D_i fix c, and there are localized coordinate slices t_j with D_i(t_j)=δ_ij and actual denominator-clearing witnesses t_j·c^n∈A. Prove the descended family is linearly independent over A.
statement:
theorem mixed_descended_linearIndependent [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
    (ι : A →ₐ[K] L) (hinj : Function.Injective ι) (c : A)
    (hu : IsUnit (ι c)) (N : I → ℕ)
    (D : I → Derivation K L L) (d : I → Derivation K A A)
    (hdesc : ∀ i a, ι (d i a) = (ι c)^(N i) * D i (ι a))
    (hfix : ∀ i, D i (ι c) = 0)
    (t : I → L) (ht : ∀ i j, D i (t j) = if i = j then 1 else 0)
    (hfrac : ∀ j, ∃ (n : ℕ) (r : A), t j * (ι c)^n = ι r) :
    LinearIndependent A d
subject: Algebraic and complex geometry
title: Prove independence after direction-dependent denominator clearing

question: For 0<δ<1/20 construct real vectors X_N with |X_Nk|≤1, a limiting normalized squared energy L≥1−7δ, and a constant C≥0 independent of N such that their normalized trigonometric polynomials have supremum at most sqrt((1+δ)^3/(1−δ))+C/N on [0,1].
statement:
theorem almost_sign_sampler {δ : ℝ} (hδ : 0<δ) (hδ20 : δ<1/20) :
    ∃ X : (N : ℕ) → Fin N → ℝ, ∃ L C : ℝ,
      0≤C ∧ 1-7*δ≤L ∧
      (∀ N : ℕ, 1≤N → ∀ k, |X N k|≤1) ∧
      Tendsto (fun N : ℕ ↦ (∑ k : Fin N, (X N k)^2)/(N : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 L) ∧
      ∀ N : ℕ, 1≤N → ∀ t∈Set.Icc (0:ℝ) 1,
        ‖(1/(Real.sqrt N : ℂ))*∑ k : Fin N, (X N k : ℂ)*realPhase (2*Real.pi*t*k)‖≤
          Real.sqrt ((1+δ)^3/(1-δ))+C/N
subject: Real and complex analysis
title: Construct almost-sign polynomials with near-unit energy and sup norm

question: For r≥2 nonzero pairwise rationally nonparallel integer row vectors a_j, natural-number slot data d, and 0<t<1/(2·periodLength(oddLengths d)), find prime q, R≥3, K>0, slot choices ω and M⊂(Z/qZ)^m such that 2KR·periodLength<q, every row evaluation of every y∈M hits its designated slot, all row evaluations distinguish distinct y,z∈M, and |M|>tq.
statement:
lemma integer_slot_matching {r m : ℕ} (hr : 2≤r)
    (a : Fin r → Fin m → ℤ)
    (ha : ∀ j, (fun k ↦ (a j k : ℚ))≠0)
    (hnp : ∀ j l, j≠l → ∀ c : ℚ,
      (fun k ↦ (a l k : ℚ))≠c • (fun k ↦ (a j k : ℚ)))
    (d : Fin r → ℕ) {t : ℝ} (ht0 : 0<t) (ht : t<1/(2*periodLength (oddLengths d) : ℝ)) :
    ∃ q R K : ℕ, q.Prime ∧ 3≤R ∧ 0<K ∧ 2*(K*(R*periodLength (oddLengths d)))<q ∧
      ∃ ω : SlotChoices d K, ∃ M : Finset (Fin m → ZMod q),
        (∀ y∈M, ∀ i, slotHit d R K q i ω (dotProduct (fun k ↦ (a i k : ZMod q)) y)) ∧
        (∀ y∈M, ∀ z∈M, y≠z → ∀ i,
          dotProduct (fun k ↦ (a i k : ZMod q)) y≠dotProduct (fun k ↦ (a i k : ZMod q)) z) ∧
        t*q<(M.card : ℝ)
subject: Real and complex analysis
title: Prime-modulus slot matching for nonparallel integer rows

question: For r≥2 nonzero pairwise rationally nonparallel integer row vectors a_i and positive widths w_i with 2Σ_i w_i<1, construct H≥1 and phases θ_h∈(R/Z)^m so that every pair of distinctly indexed signed intervals centered at ±Σ_k a_ik θ_hk, with width w_i/H, is disjoint. Distinct indices include the sign, row and copy: (e,i,h)≠(f,j,v). Use the pinned circleInterval convention.
statement:
theorem signed_interval_packing {r m : ℕ} (hr : 2≤r)
    (a : Fin r → Fin m → ℤ)
    (ha : ∀ j, (fun k ↦ (a j k : ℚ))≠0)
    (hnp : ∀ j l, j≠l → ∀ c : ℚ,
      (fun k ↦ (a l k : ℚ))≠c • (fun k ↦ (a j k : ℚ)))
    (w : Fin r → ℝ) (hw : ∀ i, 0<w i) (hs : 2*∑ i, w i<1) :
    ∃ H : ℕ, 1≤H ∧ ∃ θ : Fin H → Fin m → UnitAddCircle,
      ∀ e f : Bool, ∀ i j : Fin r, ∀ h v : Fin H, (e,i,h)≠(f,j,v) →
        Disjoint (circleInterval (signedCircle e (∑ k, a i k • θ h k)) (w i/H))
          (circleInterval (signedCircle f (∑ k, a j k • θ v k)) (w j/H))
subject: Real and complex analysis
title: Pack signed curvature intervals simultaneously on the circle

question: For the finite mode family g_i,c_i,λ_i,b_i,d_i in the exact statement, assume smooth compact support inside (0,1), |g_i|≤1, λ_i≠0, |c_i|/sqrt|λ_i|≤K, and the stationary locations have at most one nonzero mode/index at each t. Prove the normalized sampled mode polynomial is bounded by K+C/N uniformly for N≥1 and t∈[0,1].
statement:
theorem mode_maximum {P : Type uP} [Fintype P] (g : P → ℝ → ℂ) (c : P → ℂ)
    (lam b d : P → ℝ) (hgc : ∀ i, HasCompactSupport (g i))
    (hgs : ∀ i, ContDiff ℝ ∞ (g i)) (hgi : ∀ i, tsupport (g i)⊆Set.Ioo (0:ℝ) 1)
    (hgb : ∀ i x, ‖g i x‖≤1) (hlam : ∀ i, lam i≠0)
    {K : ℝ} (hK : 0≤K) (hc : ∀ i, ‖c i‖/Real.sqrt |lam i|≤K)
    (hsparse : ∀ t : ℝ, ∀ i j : P, ∀ l m : ℤ,
      g i (((l : ℝ)-(b i+t))/lam i)≠0 → g j (((m : ℝ)-(b j+t))/lam j)≠0 →
      i=j ∧ l=m) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0≤C ∧ ∀ N : ℕ, 1≤N → ∀ t∈Set.Icc (0:ℝ) 1,
      ‖(1/(Real.sqrt N : ℂ))*∑ k : Fin N,
        modeSum g c lam b d N k*realPhase (2*Real.pi*t*k)‖≤K+C/N
subject: Real and complex analysis
title: A uniform supremum bound for sparsely packed chirp modes

question: Given N≥1 and real X_k∈[−1,1], find ε_k∈{−1,1} such that on the entire unit circle the change in littlewoodValue is at most 196608·(1+sqrt(defectMass(X)·log(80N/defectMass(X)))). Use the pinned definition of defectMass, including its zero-defect convention in Lean.
statement:
theorem defect_rounding {N : ℕ} (hN : 1 ≤ N) (X : Fin N → ℝ)
    (hX : ∀ k, |X k| ≤ 1) :
    ∃ ε : Fin N → ℝ, IsRealSigning ε ∧
      ∀ z : ℂ, ‖z‖ = 1 →
        ‖littlewoodValue ε z - littlewoodValue X z‖ ≤
          196608 * (1 + Real.sqrt (defectMass X * Real.log (80 * N / defectMass X)))
subject: Real and complex analysis
title: Round almost-sign coefficients with a defect-sensitive uniform error

question: For a smooth compactly supported g with support in [−A,A], A,B≥0 and β≠0, find a finite integer set J and C≥0, independent of N≥1 and |b|≤B, such that all stationary waves outside J vanish and the normalized discrete chirp sum differs from the sum of stationary waves over J by at most C/N.
statement:
theorem uniform_poisson_chirp {g : ℝ → ℂ} (hg : HasCompactSupport g)
    (hgs : ContDiff ℝ ∞ g) {A B β : ℝ} (hA : 0≤A) (hB : 0≤B)
    (hsupp : tsupport g⊆Set.Icc (-A) A) (hβ : β≠0) :
    ∃ J : Finset ℤ, ∃ C : ℝ, 0≤C ∧ ∀ N b : ℝ, 1≤N → |b|≤B →
      (∀ l∉J, stationaryWave g N β b l=0) ∧
      ‖(1/(Real.sqrt N : ℂ))*(∑' k : ℤ, g ((k : ℝ)/N)*phase (β/N) (-b) k)-
        ∑ l∈J, stationaryWave g N β b l‖≤C/N
subject: Real and complex analysis
title: Uniform finite stationary-wave approximation for sampled chirps

question: For every facet a of Δ_10×Δ_10 and every u∈R^20, prove brightness(productFacet a,u)=|productVelocity(u,a)|/(9!·10!). Use the exact pinned normalization of Euclidean Hausdorff measure and brightness.
statement:
theorem productFacet_brightness (a : ProductFacetIndex) (u : Euclidean 20) :
    brightness (productFacet a) u =
      |productVelocity u a| / ((Nat.factorial 9 : ℝ) * (Nat.factorial 10 : ℝ))
subject: Convex and metric geometry
title: Compute brightness of each facet of the 20-dimensional witness

question: Writing u=(u^(1),u^(2)) in two ten-dimensional blocks, prove that the brightness of the pinned productWitness equals (Σ|u_i^(1)|+|Σu_i^(1)|+Σ|u_i^(2)|+|Σu_i^(2)|)/(2·9!·10!).
statement:
theorem productWitness_brightness (u : Euclidean 20) :
    brightness productWitness u =
      ((∑ i, |firstBlock u i|) + |∑ i, firstBlock u i| +
        (∑ i, |secondBlock u i|) + |∑ i, secondBlock u i|) /
          (2 * (Nat.factorial 9 : ℝ) * (Nat.factorial 10 : ℝ))
subject: Convex and metric geometry
title: Derive the complete brightness formula for Δ10 × Δ10

question: For distinct product-facet indices a,b and productVelocity(u,b)≠0, show that the set of y∈u⊥ satisfying v_b q_a(y)−v_a q_b(y)=0 has zero intrinsic volume, with q and v the pinned product coordinates and velocities.
statement:
theorem projected_product_facet_seam_null (u : Euclidean 20) (a b : ProductFacetIndex)
    (hab : a ≠ b) (hb : productVelocity u b ≠ 0) :
    volume {y : normalHyperplane u |
      productVelocity u b * productCoordinates y.val a -
        productVelocity u a * productCoordinates y.val b = 0} = 0
subject: Convex and metric geometry
title: Show projected product-facet seams have zero measure

question: For every p>2 prove there is C_p>0 such that, whenever A>0 and 0≤a_k≤A·2^k for k<N, (Σ_{k<N}a_k)^p≤C_p A^(p−2) Σ_{k<N}2^((p−2)k)a_k². The exact Lean statement uses inverse powers of 2^(2−p).
statement:
lemma dyadic_interpolation (p : ℝ) (hp : 2 < p) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ (N : ℕ) (A : ℝ) (a : ℕ → ℝ), 0 < A →
      (∀ k, 0 ≤ a k) → (∀ k < N, a k ≤ A*2^k) →
      (∑ k ∈ range N, a k)^p ≤ C*A^(p-2)*
        ∑ k ∈ range N, (((2:ℝ)^(2-p))^k)⁻¹ * (a k)^2
subject: Convex and metric geometry
title: A scale-sensitive interpolation inequality for dyadic ramps

question: For positive edge conductances c and weights w on the finite graph described by src,dst, assume every vertex is incident to an edge and each distinct vertex pair has an edge, as in the exact statement. Prove Σ_e,f w_e w_f |gramProjection(conductorMatrix)_ef|≤2 log|V| Σ_e w_e².
statement:
lemma graph_localization_positive (src dst : E → V) (c w : E → ℝ)
    (hc : ∀ e, 0 < c e) (hw : ∀ e, 0 < w e)
    (hinc : ∀ i : V, ∃ e, src e = i ∨ dst e = i)
    (hconn : ∀ i j : V, i ≠ j → ∃ e,
      (src e = i ∧ dst e = j) ∨ (src e = j ∧ dst e = i))
    (hW : 0 < ∑ e, (w e)^2) :
    (∑ e, ∑ f, w e * w f * |gramProjection (conductorMatrix src dst c) e f|) ≤
      2 * Real.log (Fintype.card V : ℝ) * ∑ e, (w e)^2
subject: Convex and metric geometry
title: Logarithmic weighted localization of an electrical projection

question: For p>2 and ε>0, under the pinned graph, weight and normalized gradient-family assumptions, construct a symmetric probability law ν supported in the normalized gradient range. Prove the coordinate bound H·2^(2ℓ), the weighted p-moment approximation εb+C H^(p−2)ℓ, and both weighted and coordinatewise second-moment bounds in the exact statement (H=4log|V|, N=|I| and b the Pareto ramp moment).
statement:
lemma ramp_jump_law (p ε : ℝ) (hp : 2 < p) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ (E : Type uE) (V : Type uV) (I : Type uI) [Fintype E] [Fintype V] [Fintype I]
      [DecidableEq E] [DecidableEq V] [Nonempty E] [Nonempty I]
      (src dst : E → V) (δ w : E → ℝ) (_hδ : ∀ e, 0 < δ e)
      (_hw : ∀ e, 0 < w e) (_hws : ∑ e, w e=1)
      (_hcard : 2 ≤ Fintype.card V)
      (_hinc : ∀ i : V, ∃ e, src e=i ∨ dst e=i)
      (_hconn : ∀ i j : V, i ≠ j → ∃ e,
        (src e=i ∧ dst e=j) ∨ (src e=j ∧ dst e=i))
      (g : I → E → ℝ) (_hg : ∀ e, ∑ i, |g i e|^p=1)
      (_hgr : ∀ i, ∃ x, (normalizedGradient src dst δ).mulVec x=g i)
      (ℓ : ℕ),
      let H := 4*Real.log (Fintype.card V : ℝ)
      let N := (Fintype.card I : ℝ)
      let b := ∫ r, |dyadicRamp ℓ r|^p ∂pareto p
      ∃ ν : Measure (E → ℝ), IsProbabilityMeasure ν ∧ ν.map (fun v => -v)=ν ∧
        (∀ᵐ z ∂ν, ∃ x, (normalizedGradient src dst δ).mulVec x=z) ∧
        (∀ᵐ z ∂ν, ∀ e, |z e| ≤ H*2^(2*ℓ)) ∧
        (∑ e, w e*|N*(∫ z, |z e|^p ∂ν)-b|) ≤ ε*b+C*H^(p-2)*(ℓ:ℝ) ∧
        (∑ e, w e*(N*(∫ z, (z e)^2 ∂ν))) ≤ 4*aboveVariance p ∧
        (∀ e, N*(∫ z, (z e)^2 ∂ν) ≤ H^2*aboveVariance p)
subject: Convex and metric geometry
title: Construct a symmetric bounded jump law in the gradient range

question: For p>2, prove a uniform constant C_p bounds the weighted expected pth power of P applied to a dyadic ramp minus that ramp by C_p H^(p−2) ℓ B. Assume P has row norm≤H, fixes the random vector almost surely, the stated dyadic tail second moments and their projected weighted moments are bounded, and weights are nonnegative and sum to 1.
statement:
lemma ramp_projection_error (p : ℝ) (hp : 2 < p) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ (E : Type uE) [Fintype E]
      (μ : Measure (E → ℝ)) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
      (P : Matrix E E ℝ) (w : E → ℝ) (_hw : ∀ e, 0 ≤ w e) (_hws : ∑ e, w e=1)
      (H B : ℝ) (_hH : 1 ≤ H) (_hB : 0 ≤ B) (ℓ : ℕ),
      (∀ e, matrixRowNorm P e ≤ H) →
      (∀ᵐ v ∂μ, P.mulVec v=v) →
      (∀ k < 2*ℓ, ∀ e, Integrable (fun v => (tailPart ((2:ℝ)^k) (v e))^2) μ) →
      (∀ k < 2*ℓ, ∀ e, (∫ v, (tailPart ((2:ℝ)^k) (v e))^2 ∂μ) ≤ B*((2:ℝ)^(2-p))^k) →
      (∀ k < 2*ℓ, (∑ e, w e*(∫ v, (P.mulVec (fun a => tailPart ((2:ℝ)^k) (v a)) e)^2 ∂μ)) ≤
        4*B*((2:ℝ)^(2-p))^k) →
      (∑ e, w e*(∫ v, |P.mulVec (fun a => dyadicRamp ℓ (v a)) e-dyadicRamp ℓ (v e)|^p ∂μ)) ≤
        C*H^(p-2)*(ℓ:ℝ)*B
subject: Convex and metric geometry
title: Control projected ramp error using quadratic tails

question: Let 1<p<2, c>0 and μ be a probability law with real characteristic function exp(−c|t|^p). Given the exact complete-edge graph assumptions, positive normalized weights lam, and a random normalized gradient Y with every coordinate law μ, construct measurable gradient-valued F bounded coordinatewise by 4 log|V|·T. Prove the explicit weighted p-moment approximation to the clipped μ moment stated in Lean, including its T^(1−p) and T^(2−p) error terms.
statement:
lemma stable_retraction_moments {Ω : Type uΩ} {E : Type uE} {V : Type uV} [MeasurableSpace Ω]
    [Fintype E] [Fintype V] [DecidableEq E] [DecidableEq V] [Nonempty E]
    (ν : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure ν] (μ : Measure ℝ) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    (p c : ℝ) (hp : 1 < p) (hp2 : p < 2) (hc : 0 < c)
    (hcf : ∀ t : ℝ, (charFun μ t).re = Real.exp (-c*|t|^p))
    (src dst : E → V) (δ lam : E → ℝ) (hδ : ∀ e, 0 < δ e)
    (hlam : ∀ e, 0 < lam e) (hls : ∑ e, lam e = 1)
    (hcard : 2 ≤ Fintype.card V)
    (hinc : ∀ i : V, ∃ e, src e = i ∨ dst e = i)
    (hconn : ∀ i j : V, i ≠ j → ∃ e,
      (src e = i ∧ dst e = j) ∨ (src e = j ∧ dst e = i))
    (Y : Ω → E → ℝ) (hm : Measurable Y)
    (hY : ∀ x, ∃ z, (normalizedGradient src dst δ).mulVec z = Y x)
    (hLaw : ∀ e, ν.map (fun x => Y x e) = μ)
    (T a : ℝ) (hT : 0 < T) (ha : 0 < a) :
    ∃ F : Ω → E → ℝ, Measurable F ∧
      (∀ x, ∃ z, (normalizedGradient src dst δ).mulVec z = F x) ∧
      (∀ x e, |F x e| ≤ (4*Real.log (Fintype.card V:ℝ))*T) ∧
      (∑ e, lam e*|(∫ x, |F x e|^p ∂ν)-(∫ x, (min |x| a)^p ∂μ)|) ≤
        (p*a^(p-1))*(4*Real.log (Fintype.card V:ℝ))*
          ((2*c*2^p)*(1+1/(p-1))*T^(1-p))+
        a^(p-2)*(96*c*T^(2-p))
subject: Convex and metric geometry
title: Bounded gradient retraction with stable-law moment control

question: For a finite loopless multigraph, contract the complement of S on one side and S on the other, retaining edge identities. Given probability laws on the two contracted perfect-matching spaces whose edge marginals are restrictions of the same x, construct a probability law on original perfect matchings with marginals x.
statement:
theorem couple_laws (G : LooplessGraph V E) (S : Finset V) (x : E → ℝ)
    {p : (G.onSide S).Matching → ℝ} {q : (G.onSide Sᶜ).Matching → ℝ}
    (hp : p ∈ probabilitySimplex (G.onSide S).Matching)
    (hq : q ∈ probabilitySimplex (G.onSide Sᶜ).Matching)
    (hpx : ∀ e, (G.onSide S).mean p e = x e.val)
    (hqx : ∀ e, (G.onSide Sᶜ).mean q e = x e.val) :
    ∃ r, r ∈ G.feasibleLaws x
subject: Theoretical computer science
title: Coupling matching laws across a contracted cut

question: At a feasible point x in an even-order graph and a tight odd cut S of mass one, suppose a direction on the positive edge support restricts to the face spaces of both contracted sides. Prove it lies in the original face space, including active cuts crossing S.
statement:
theorem faceSpace_of_side_spaces (G : LooplessGraph V E) {x : E → ℝ}
    (heven : Even (Fintype.card V)) (hx : x ∈ G.constraintPolytope)
    (S : Finset V) (hS : Odd S.card) (ht : G.cutMass x S=1)
    {u : {e // 0<x e} → ℝ}
    (h1 : G.sideRestriction x S u ∈ (G.onSide S).faceSpace (G.sideMarginal x S))
    (h2 : G.sideRestriction x Sᶜ u ∈ (G.onSide Sᶜ).faceSpace (G.sideMarginal x Sᶜ)) :
    u ∈ G.faceSpace x
subject: Theoretical computer science
title: Gluing tangent directions across tight odd cuts

question: For every finite loopless multigraph of even order n≥4 and every point of its constraint polytope, prove the positive-support face codimension is at most 2(n−2).
statement:
theorem faceCodimension_strong_aux (n : ℕ) :
    ∀ {W F : Type*} [Fintype W] [Fintype F] [DecidableEq W] [DecidableEq F]
      (G : LooplessGraph W F), Fintype.card W=n → Even n → 4≤n →
      ∀ x ∈ G.constraintPolytope, G.faceCodimension x ≤ 2*(n-2)
subject: Theoretical computer science
title: Inductive bound on matching-face codimension

question: At an entropy-defect maximizer with optimizing law p and m>0, let C be the covariance of matching indicators normalized on the positive marginal support. Prove (8 exp(−H(x)/m)−1)·||Cu||² + uᵀCu ≤ 0 for every vector u.
statement:
theorem matching_covariance_second_variation (G : LooplessGraph V E) {x : E → ℝ}
    {p : G.Matching → ℝ} (hp : p ∈ G.feasibleLaws x)
    (hopt : entropy p=maxMatchingEntropy G x) {m : ℝ} (hm : 0 < m)
    (hmax : ∀ y ∈ G.polytope, entropyDefect G m y ≤ entropyDefect G m x)
    (u : {e // 0 < x e} → ℝ) :
    (8*Real.exp (-entropy x/m)-1)*
        ((covariance p (matchingNormalized G x) *ᵥ u) ⬝ᵥ
          (covariance p (matchingNormalized G x) *ᵥ u)) +
      u ⬝ᵥ (covariance p (matchingNormalized G x) *ᵥ u) ≤ 0
subject: Theoretical computer science
title: From entropy variation to a covariance inequality

question: Let p maximize matching entropy among laws with marginals x, and let x maximize the supplied entropyDefect over the matching polytope. For every centered linear matching score, derive the displayed second-variation inequality combining weighted squared marginal motion, the squared entropy derivative, and the score variance.
statement:
theorem matching_defect_second_variation (G : LooplessGraph V E) {x : E → ℝ}
    {p : G.Matching → ℝ} (hp : p ∈ G.feasibleLaws x)
    (hopt : entropy p = maxMatchingEntropy G x) {m : ℝ} (hm : m ≠ 0)
    (hmax : ∀ y ∈ G.polytope, entropyDefect G m y ≤ entropyDefect G m x)
    (u : E → ℝ) (c : ℝ) (hcenter : ∑ M, p M*linearScore G u c M = 0) :
    (8*Real.exp (-entropy x/m)-1)*
        (∑ e, (G.mean (fun M => p M*linearScore G u c M) e)^2/x e) +
      (8*Real.exp (-entropy x/m)/m)*
        (entropyLineD x (G.mean (fun M => p M*linearScore G u c M)) 0)^2 +
      (∑ M, p M*(linearScore G u c M)^2) ≤ 0
subject: Theoretical computer science
title: Second variation of the actual matching entropy defect

question: Let p₀,p,Q,S be formal power series over a characteristic-zero field, with p₀≠0 and Q(0)≠0. If (XQ)(p₀p′−p₀′p)+p₀²S=0, prove S(0)=0.
statement:
theorem formal_residue_obstruction (p0 p Q S : PowerSeries F)
    (hp0 : p0 ≠ 0) (hQ : PowerSeries.constantCoeff Q ≠ 0)
    (h : (PowerSeries.X * Q) *
        (p0 * PowerSeries.derivative (R := F) p - PowerSeries.derivative (R := F) p0 * p) +
        p0^2 * S = 0) : PowerSeries.constantCoeff S = 0
subject: Theoretical computer science
title: Formal residue obstruction from a Wronskian relation

question: Over a commutative domain, assume ZG=DH, H=WC, W=HE, G is invertible, and det(D),det(W) are nonzero. Prove there is a square column minor of Z with nonzero determinant divisible by det(W), as specified in the exact matrix-shaped statement.
statement:
theorem exists_nonzero_divisible_minor
    (Z H : Matrix K I R) (G : Matrix I I R) (D W : Matrix K K R)
    (C : Matrix K I R) (E : Matrix I K R)
    (hG : IsUnit G) (hD : D.det ≠ 0) (hW : W.det ≠ 0)
    (hZG : Z * G = D * H) (hHC : H = W * C) (hHE : W = H * E) :
    ∃ f : K → I, (Z.submatrix id f).det ≠ 0 ∧ W.det ∣ (Z.submatrix id f).det
subject: Theoretical computer science
title: Extract a nonzero minor carrying the Wronskian factor

question: Given the polynomial differential system qG′=PG, the invertible formal fundamental matrix G, deg(q)≤n, deg(P_tl)≤n−1, and a nonzero scalar output uᵀGv, prove its order is strictly below (n−1)·choose(|I|,2)+|I|.
statement:
theorem system_multiplicity (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n)
    (q : F[X]) (P : Matrix I I F[X]) (u v : I → F)
    (G : Matrix I I (PowerSeries F))
    (hq : q.natDegree ≤ n) (hqn : q ≠ 0)
    (hP : ∀ t l, (P t l).natDegree ≤ n-1) (hG : IsUnit G)
    (hD : ∀ t l, (q : PowerSeries F) * PowerSeries.derivative (R := F) (G t l) =
      ∑ a : I, (P t a : PowerSeries F) * G a l)
    (hy : systemScalarOutput u v G ≠ 0) :
    (systemScalarOutput u v G).order.toNat <
      (n-1) * (Fintype.card I).choose 2 + Fintype.card I
subject: Theoretical computer science
title: Bound vanishing order of a nonzero differential-system output

question: For an AcyclicRepresentation R, prove that its finite formal-series fundamentalMatrix satisfies G′=R.systemMatrix·G entrywise.
statement:
theorem fundamentalMatrix_derivative (R : AcyclicRepresentation F n) :
    R.fundamentalMatrix.map (PowerSeries.derivative (R := F)) =
      R.systemMatrix * R.fundamentalMatrix
subject: Theoretical computer science
title: The finite acyclic series construction solves its matrix ODE

question: Assume the stated differential recurrence for every prefixed wordSeries. Show that encoding polynomialTransform(q,p₀,Q,c) equals q·(p₀·(polynomialEncode c)′−p₀′·polynomialEncode c).
statement:
theorem polynomialEncode_transform (q p0 : F[X]) (Q : Fin n → F[X])
    (hq : ∀ (i : Fin n) (w : List (Fin n)),
      (q : PowerSeries F) * PowerSeries.derivative (R := F) (wordSeries (i :: w)) =
        (Q i : PowerSeries F) * wordSeries w)
    (c : PolyWords F n) :
    polynomialEncode (polynomialTransform q p0 Q c) =
      (q : PowerSeries F) * ((p0 : PowerSeries F) *
        PowerSeries.derivative (R := F) (polynomialEncode c) -
          (p0.derivative : PowerSeries F) * polynomialEncode c)
subject: Theoretical computer science
title: Differentiate the polynomial word encoding by an explicit coefficient transform

question: For a finitely supported polynomial coefficient function c on words in Fin n whose nonzero words have length at most D, prove that polynomialEncode(c)=0 forces c=0.
statement:
theorem polynomialEncode_eq_zero (D : ℕ) (c : PolyWords F n)
    (hc : LengthBound D c) (he : polynomialEncode c = 0) : c = 0
subject: Theoretical computer science
title: Eliminate every bounded polynomial relation among word series

question: Assuming the monotonicity/support properties of L and r and the two displayed dissipation bounds, prove informationDeficit(noiseFlow(F,t))≤psi(exp(−t)) for every t>0 and nonconstant increasing sign-valued F.
statement:
theorem informationDeficit_noiseFlow_le_psi_from_dissipation
    (hLmono : AntitoneOn L (Ioi 0))
    (hLsupport : ∀ x, 0 < x → ∀ y, 0 < y → L x + LDeriv x * (y - x) ≤ L y)
    (hrmono : MonotoneOn r (Ico 0 ell))
    {n : ℕ}
    (hmonoD : ∀ g : Cube n → ℝ, IsInterior g → IsIncreasing g →
      2 * informationDeficit g + meanVariance g * L (entropyAverage g / meanVariance g) ≤
        dissipation g)
    (hsmallD : ∀ g : Cube n → ℝ, IsInterior g → informationDeficit g ≤ s0 →
      r (informationDeficit g) ≤ dissipation g)
    (F : Cube n → ℝ) (hF : IsSignValued F) (hinc : IsIncreasing F)
    (hnc : ∃ x y, F x ≠ F y) {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 < t) :
    informationDeficit (noiseFlow F t) ≤ psi (Real.exp (-t))
subject: Theoretical computer science
title: Join the large- and small-information flow regimes

question: Assume the stated convexity, increment, and two-point bounds for K. Prove that every interior real-valued function g on the Boolean n-cube satisfies 2·informationDeficit(g)+K(informationDeficit(g)) ≤ dissipation(g).
statement:
theorem general_dissipation_of_K_estimates
    (hconvex : ConvexOn ℝ (Ici 0) K)
    (hincrement : ∀ {Je Jm Sa : ℝ}, 0 ≤ Jm → Jm ≤ Je → 0 ≤ Sa →
      K (Je + Sa) - K (Je + Sa - Jm) ≤ K Je + Jm * Sa / ell)
    (hpoint : ∀ (a b : ℝ), |a| + |b| < 1 →
      K (pairEntropyGap a b) ≤ pairDissipation a b - 2 * pairEntropyGap a b) :
    ∀ {n : ℕ} (g : Cube n → ℝ), IsInterior g →
      2 * informationDeficit g + K (informationDeficit g) ≤ dissipation g
subject: Theoretical computer science
title: Lift scalar dissipation estimates to every cube dimension

question: For probability weights w and pairs (a_i,b_i) satisfying |a_i|+|b_i|<1 and b_i≥0, prove the displayed lower bound on twice the Jensen gap of pairEntropyGap by the rational variance gap multiplied by lambda((weightedMean(b)/(1+|weightedMean(a)|))²).
statement:
theorem weighted_pair_jensen_gap_strengthened (w a b : ι → ℝ)
    (hw : ∀ i, 0 ≤ w i) (hprob : ∑ i, w i = 1)
    (hdom : ∀ i, |a i| + |b i| < 1) (hb : ∀ i, 0 ≤ b i) :
    ((∑ i, w i * (b i) ^ 2 / (1 - (a i) ^ 2)) -
      (∑ i, w i * b i) ^ 2 / (1 - (∑ i, w i * a i) ^ 2)) *
        lambda (((∑ i, w i * b i) / (1 + |∑ i, w i * a i|)) ^ 2) ≤
      2 * ((∑ i, w i * pairEntropyGap (a i) (b i)) -
        pairEntropyGap (∑ i, w i * a i) (∑ i, w i * b i))
subject: Theoretical computer science
title: A strengthened weighted two-point entropy gap

question: From the stated convexity of L, normalized two-point bound, and three-parameter perspective inequality, prove the displayed dissipation lower bound for every increasing interior g on every Boolean cube.
statement:
theorem monotone_dissipation_from_scalar_lemmas
    (hconvex : ConvexOn ℝ (Ioi 0) L)
    (hpair : ∀ a b : ℝ, |a| + |b| < 1 →
      (1 - a ^ 2) * L (((entropy (a + b) + entropy (a - b)) / 2) / (1 - a ^ 2)) ≤
        pairDissipation a b - 2 * pairEntropyGap a b)
    (hperspective : ∀ x w q : ℝ, 0 < x → 0 < w → w ≤ 1 → 0 ≤ q → q < 1 → q ≤ w ^ 2 →
      L x - (1 - q) * L (x / (1 - q)) - w * L (x / w) ≤
        q * (1 / w - 1) * lambda (q ^ 2)) :
    ∀ {n : ℕ} (g : Cube n → ℝ), IsInterior g → IsIncreasing g →
      2 * informationDeficit g + meanVariance g * L (entropyAverage g / meanVariance g) ≤
        dissipation g
subject: Theoretical computer science
title: Lift a perspective inequality to monotone cube dissipation

question: For |a|+|b|<1 and |v|<1 satisfying psi(v)=pairEntropyGap(a,b)/(1−a²), prove v·artanh(v)≤pairDissipation(a,b)/(1−a²).
statement:
theorem normalized_pair_dissipation_ge_of_psi {a b v : ℝ}
    (hab : |a| + |b| < 1) (hv : |v| < 1)
    (hvpsi : psi v = pairEntropyGap a b / (1 - a ^ 2)) :
    v * Real.artanh v ≤ pairDissipation a b / (1 - a ^ 2)
subject: Theoretical computer science
title: Compare normalized pair dissipation at equal entropy

question: For sign-valued F on the Boolean cube, noise parameter u∈[0,1], coordinate i, and point x, prove that the sum of psi at the two noisy coordinate values does not decrease when F is sorted along i, as in the exact statement.
statement:
theorem psi_noise_sortCoordinate_pair (i : Fin n) {u : ℝ}
    (hu : u ∈ Set.Icc 0 1) {F : Cube n → ℝ} (hF : IsSignValued F) (x : Cube n) :
    psi (noiseOperator u F (setBit i false x)) +
        psi (noiseOperator u F (setBit i true x)) ≤
      psi (noiseOperator u (sortCoordinate i F) (setBit i false x)) +
        psi (noiseOperator u (sortCoordinate i F) (setBit i true x))
subject: Theoretical computer science
title: Coordinate sorting increases the noisy pair entropy functional

question: Let a Boolean seed f reject zero, have sensitivity at most A>1, and zero-input block sensitivity at least B>A². For alpha=log B/log A, prove alpha>2, every iterated composition is nonconstant and has block sensitivity at least sensitivity^alpha, the quadratic ratio grows at least as (B/A²)^m, and zero-input block sensitivity diverges.
statement:
theorem power_amplification {I : Type} [Fintype I]
    (f : (I → Bool) → Bool) (hf : f (fun _ => false) = false)
    (A B : ℕ) (hs : sensitivity f ≤ A)
    (hb : B ≤ blockSensitivityAt f (fun _ => false))
    (hA : 1 < A) (hB : A ^ 2 < B) :
    let α := Real.log (B : ℝ) / Real.log (A : ℝ)
    2 < α ∧
      (∀ m : ℕ,
        0 < Fintype.card I ^ m ∧
        iterateFin f m (fun _ => false) = false ∧
        (∃ x y, iterateFin f m x ≠ iterateFin f m y) ∧
        (sensitivity (iterateFin f m) : ℝ) ^ α ≤
          (blockSensitivityAt (iterateFin f m) (fun _ => false) : ℝ) ∧
        ((B : ℝ) / (A : ℝ) ^ 2) ^ m ≤
          (blockSensitivity (iterateFin f m) : ℝ) /
            (sensitivity (iterateFin f m) : ℝ) ^ 2) ∧
      Filter.Tendsto
        (fun m : ℕ => (blockSensitivityAt (iterateFin f m) (fun _ => false) : ℝ))
        Filter.atTop Filter.atTop
subject: Theoretical computer science
title: Amplifying a seed gap beyond quadratic sensitivity

question: For q<q' in a nested recursive family, suppose both parent predicates reject the same input. Prove the number of single-bit flips changing both is at most 16 times false-side child sensitivity plus three times true joint child sensitivity.
statement:
theorem recursive_joint_zero_at {k r h : ℕ} {I : Type} [Fintype I]
    (T : Tournament k) (A : GoodLabeling T r)
    (F : Fin (h + 1) → (I → Bool) → Bool) (hF : NestedFamily F) (hr : 0 < r)
    (q q' : Fin h) (hqq : q < q') (x : ((Fin k × Fin r) × I) → Bool)
    (hx : recursiveFamily T A.label F q x = false)
    (hx' : recursiveFamily T A.label F q' x = false) :
    jointSensitivityAt (recursiveFamily T A.label F q) (recursiveFamily T A.label F q') x ≤
      16 * sideSensitivity F false + 3 * jointSensitivity F true
subject: Theoretical computer science
title: Joint zero-side sensitivity across two thresholds

question: In a tournament with common out-degree o, consider a nested child family and q<q' such that both recursive parent predicates accept x. Prove joint sensitivity at x is at most o times false joint child sensitivity plus r times true-side child sensitivity.
statement:
theorem recursive_joint_one_at {k r h : ℕ} {I : Type} [Fintype I]
    (T : Tournament k) (label : Fin k → Fin k → Fin r)
    (F : Fin (h + 1) → (I → Bool) → Bool) (hF : NestedFamily F) (o : ℕ)
    (ho : ∀ i, (Finset.univ.filter (T.Adj i)).card = o)
    (q q' : Fin h) (hqq : q < q') (x : ((Fin k × Fin r) × I) → Bool)
    (hx : recursiveFamily T label F q x = true)
    (hx' : recursiveFamily T label F q' x = true) :
    jointSensitivityAt (recursiveFamily T label F q) (recursiveFamily T label F q') x ≤
      o * jointSensitivity F false + r * sideSensitivity F true
subject: Theoretical computer science
title: Joint one-side sensitivity across two thresholds

question: In the tournament-labeled recursive Boolean construction, a single raw bit flip changes row i from false to true. Prove exactly one of the stated repair modes holds: it fixes the unique failed target on row i, or it fixes the unique failed gate on an outgoing neighbor with the required label; include the candidate memberships and before/after child values.
statement:
theorem rowClause_repair_cases {k r h : ℕ} {I : Type} (T : Tournament k)
    (label : Fin k → Fin k → Fin r) (F : Fin (h + 1) → (I → Bool) → Bool)
    (q : Fin h) (x : ((Fin k × Fin r) × I) → Bool)
    (i j : Fin k) (c : Fin r) (a : I)
    (hi : rowClause T label F q x i = false)
    (hf : rowClause T label F q (flip x {((j, c), a)}) i = true) :
    (i ∈ targetCandidates T label F q x ∧ j = i ∧
      F (Fin.last h) (recursiveChild x j c) = false ∧
      F (Fin.last h) (flip (recursiveChild x j c) {a}) = true) ∨
    (i ∈ gateCandidates T label F q x ∧ T.Adj i j ∧ c = label i j ∧
      F (gateIndex q) (recursiveChild x j c) = true ∧
      F (gateIndex q) (flip (recursiveChild x j c) {a}) = false)
subject: Theoretical computer science
title: Classifying single-bit repairs of recursive clauses

question: For a nested child family F and good tournament labeling A, at an input where recursiveFamily q is false, prove its sensitivity is at most 16 times F's false-side sensitivity plus its true-side sensitivity plus three times its true joint sensitivity.
statement:
theorem recursive_sensitivity_zero_at {k r h : ℕ} {I : Type} [Fintype I]
    (T : Tournament k) (A : GoodLabeling T r)
    (F : Fin (h + 1) → (I → Bool) → Bool) (hF : NestedFamily F) (hr : 0 < r)
    (q : Fin h) (x : ((Fin k × Fin r) × I) → Bool)
    (hx : recursiveFamily T A.label F q x = false) :
    sensitivityAt (recursiveFamily T A.label F q) x ≤
      16 * sideSensitivity F false + sideSensitivity F true + 3 * jointSensitivity F true
subject: Theoretical computer science
title: Zero-side sensitivity from target and gate repairs

question: For an arc-minimal oriented counterexample r to the second-neighborhood inequality, set E=N⁺(S)\S and let T be a proper subset of E. Prove there is a nonempty Q contained in E\T such that the supplied deficitPotential of T union Q grows by strictly less than |Q|.
statement:
theorem deficitPotential_step (r : V → V → Prop) (hr : IsOriented r)
    (hcounter : Counterexample r) (hminimal : ArcMinimal r)
    (S T : Finset V) (hT : T ⊆ image r S \ S)
    (hproper : T ≠ image r S \ S) :
    ∃ Q : Finset V, Q.Nonempty ∧ Q ⊆ (image r S \ S) \ T ∧
      deficitPotential r S (T ∪ Q) < deficitPotential r S T + Q.card
subject: Combinatorics
title: A deficit-improving step by arc deletion

question: Given maximum support matchings alpha and beta for the supplied pruning matrices L and N-transpose, choose one real coefficient assignment that is supported on r, satisfies all local maximal-rank conditions, makes both matching minors nonzero, and realizes ranks |alpha| and |beta| simultaneously.
statement:
theorem exists_pruning_rank_coefficients
    (r : X → X → Prop) (R C : Finset (X × X))
    (α : Finset (↥(Z r R C) × ↥R)) (β : Finset (↥(Z r R C) × ↥C))
    (hα : IsMaximumMatching (matrixLSupport r R C) α)
    (hβ : IsMaximumMatching (matrixNTransposeSupport r R C) β) :
    ∃ v : CoefficientVariables X → ℝ,
      SupportedCoefficients r (selectedA r v) ∧
      SupportedCoefficients r (selectedB r v) ∧
      LocalMaximalRanks r R C (selectedB r v) ∧
      ((matrixL r R C (selectedA r v)).submatrix
        (fun e : ↥α => e.1.1) (fun e : ↥α => e.1.2)).det ≠ 0 ∧
      (((matrixN r R C (selectedB r v))ᵀ).submatrix
        (fun e : ↥β => e.1.1) (fun e : ↥β => e.1.2)).det ≠ 0 ∧
      (matrixL r R C (selectedA r v)).rank = α.card ∧
      ((matrixN r R C (selectedB r v))ᵀ).rank = β.card
subject: Combinatorics
title: Simultaneous coefficient selection for pruning ranks

question: In a finite bipartite graph, every edge entering Q on the right comes from P on the left. Among all maximum matchings let M minimize the number of P-to-complement-Q edges. Prove the restriction of M to right endpoints in Q is a maximum matching for that restricted edge relation.
statement:
theorem isMaximumMatching_rightBlock_of_minimum_crossing
    (P : L → Prop) (Q : R → Prop) [DecidablePred P] [DecidablePred Q]
    (hblock : ∀ a b, E a b → Q b → P a)
    {M : Finset (L × R)} (hM : IsMaximumMatching E M)
    (hmin : ∀ N : Finset (L × R), IsMaximumMatching E N →
      (M.filter (fun e => P e.1 ∧ ¬Q e.2)).card ≤
        (N.filter (fun e => P e.1 ∧ ¬Q e.2)).card) :
    IsMaximumMatching (fun a b => E a b ∧ Q b)
      (M.filter (fun e => Q e.2))
subject: Combinatorics
title: Block optimality of a minimum-crossing matching

question: For the supplied corner-indexed pruning matrices N and L and two coefficient functions supported on r, prove that every (right,left) entry of N·L equals a(left.first,right.first) times b(right.second,left.second).
statement:
theorem matrixN_mul_matrixL_apply
    (r : X → X → Prop) (R C : Finset (X × X)) (a b : X → X → ℝ)
    (ha : SupportedCoefficients r a) (hb : SupportedCoefficients r b)
    (right : {right : X × X // right ∈ C})
    (left : {left : X × X // left ∈ R}) :
    (matrixN r R C b * matrixL r R C a) right left =
      a left.val.1 right.val.1 * b right.val.2 left.val.2
subject: Combinatorics
title: The unique-corner sparse matrix product identity

question: For an oriented relation with positive indegree and the supplied SubsetDeficit property, replace every vertex by a transitive fiber of size m>|V|. Prove StrictSubsetGrowth for the resulting blowup relation on V×Fin m.
subject: Combinatorics
title: Strict subset growth under transitive blowup

question: Given a predecessor rule on subsets of H that supplies S subset I with 17|S|<|I| for every nonempty I subset H, construct a finite nested hierarchy starting at the empty set, ending at H, and satisfying the predecessor relation and 17-fold strict cardinal growth at every stage.
statement:
theorem exists_setHierarchy {X : Type*} [DecidableEq X]
    (R : Finset X → Finset X → Prop) (H : Finset X)
    (hpred : ∀ I, I ⊆ H → I.Nonempty →
      ∃ S, S ⊆ I ∧ 17 * S.card < I.card ∧ R S I) :
    Nonempty (SetHierarchy R H)
subject: Combinatorics
title: Constructing a sparse predecessor hierarchy

question: For a positive spread law on sets of size at most m and 0<rho<1 with a/rho≤exp(−50), prove the actual resampling probability of density at least exp(−10m) and a residual target fragment larger than m/2 is at most exp(10m)·2^m·exp(−25m).
statement:
theorem resampling_large_fragment_bound (ν : FiniteLaw B) (A : B → Finset X)
    {ρ a : ℝ} (hν : ν.IsPositive) (hρ : 0 < ρ) (hρ1 : ρ < 1)
    (m : ℕ) (hsize : ∀ b, (A b).card ≤ m) (hspread : IsSpread ν A a)
    (ha : 0 ≤ a) (hratio : a / ρ ≤ Real.exp (-50)) :
    bernoulliExpectation ρ (fun W => (resamplingLaw ν A ρ W hν hρ).prob
      (fun cb => Real.exp (-10 * (m : ℝ)) ≤
          resamplingZ ν A ρ (resamplingY A W cb.1) ∧
        m / 2 < (A cb.2 \ W).card)) ≤
      Real.exp (10 * (m : ℝ)) * (2 : ℝ) ^ m * Real.exp (-25 * (m : ℝ))
subject: Combinatorics
title: Bounding large residual fragments after resampling

question: For the supplied resampling transition, a fixed target b, positive density cutoff delta, and a nonnegative observable f depending only on coordinates outside A(b), prove its cutoff-target weighted Bernoulli expectation is bounded by delta⁻¹·nu(b)·E[f] times the inverse-probability moment of |A(c) intersection A(b)|.
statement:
theorem outside_change_of_measure_moment (ν : FiniteLaw B) (A : B → Finset X)
    {p δ : ℝ} (hp : 0 < p) (hp1 : p ≤ 1) (hδ : 0 < δ)
    (b : B) (f : Finset X → ℝ) (hf : ∀ W, 0 ≤ f W)
    (hloc : DependsOutside (A b) f) :
    bernoulliExpectation p (fun W => cutoffTargetMass ν A p δ W b * f W) ≤
      δ⁻¹ * ν.weight b * bernoulliExpectation p f *
        ν.expectation (fun c => (p⁻¹) ^ (A c ∩ A b).card)
subject: Combinatorics
title: Outside-coordinate change of measure for resampling

question: For a positive-depth covering state, suppose a recovered probability tree has halved level capacities, the required disjointness, and the reduced spread reserve. Construct a next covering state that strictly advances after adding W to the seen set.
statement:
theorem exists_advance_of_halved (state : CoverState original σ) (W : Finset X)
    (hdepth : state.depth ≠ 0) (U : ProbabilityTree X state.depth)
    (hdisjoint : U.IsDisjoint)
    (hcapacity : U.HasCapacities (fun i => state.capacity i / 2))
    (hspread : U.HasSpread (fun i => capacityReserve σ (state.capacity i / 2)))
    (hrecovery : Recovers state.tree U W) :
    ∃ next, state.Advances W next
subject: Combinatorics
title: Strict covering-state progress after capacity halving

question: For a disjoint probability tree with positive level capacities m, level spread a, and a(j)/p≤exp(−50), prove the expected recursively defined treePotential under the single shared Bernoulli set is bounded by potentialEnvelope(depth,m).
statement:
theorem treePotential_expectation_le {p : ℝ} (hp : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1)
    (m : ℕ → ℕ) (a : ℕ → ℝ) {d : ℕ} (T : ProbabilityTree X d)
    (hdis : T.IsDisjoint) (hcap : T.HasCapacities m) (hspread : T.HasSpread a)
    (hm : ∀ j, j < d → 1 ≤ m j) (ha : ∀ j, j < d → 0 ≤ a j)
    (hsmall : ∀ j, j < d → a j / p ≤ Real.exp (-50)) :
    bernoulliExpectation p (fun W => treePotential p m W T) ≤ potentialEnvelope d m
subject: Combinatorics
title: Expected potential for a dependent probability tree

question: For an opposite cycle C of a triangular incidence state s and a partner state r, replace r's chosen corner by the third corner on the faces of C and leave other faces alone. Prove this changed vertex assignment equals the original assignment after some permutation of all faces.
statement:
theorem changed_assignment_permutation (r : T.State X) (hrs : T.Partner r s) :
    ∃ e : Equiv.Perm A, ∀ t, T.vertex t (C.changedCorners r t) = r.value (e t)
subject: Combinatorics
title: Cycle reversal as a global face permutation

question: For a finite network with a bipartition black and equal numbers of black and white vertices, let H be an edge set whose restricted boundary map is injective. Suppose the H-degree of the distinguished black root is one and that of every other black vertex is two. Prove H contains an edge set P meeting every vertex exactly once.
statement:
lemma tree_matching (black : V → Prop)
    (hc : ∀ e, black (N.tail e) ↔ ¬black (N.head e))
    (H : Finset E) (hi : Function.Injective (N.restrict (Subtype.val : H → E)).boundary)
    (root : V) (_hr : black root)
    (hd : ∀ v, black v → ((N.star v).filter (fun e => e ∈ H)).card = if v = root then 1 else 2)
    (hbal : Fintype.card {v // black v} = Fintype.card {v // ¬black v}) :
    ∃ P : Finset E, P ⊆ H ∧ ∀ v, ((N.star v).filter fun e => e ∈ P).card = 1
subject: Combinatorics
title: Perfect matching from a rooted bipartite forest

question: For a simple cubic three-edge-connected network split by a three-edge cut into shores of at least two vertices, suppose each capped shore has a perfect matching with connected complement and their boundary matching choices agree. Prove the complement of the union of the two lifted matchings is connected in the original network.
statement:
lemma cap_glue_connected (hN : N.Simple) (hc : N.graph.IsRegularOfDegree 3)
    (h3 : N.ThreeEdgeConnected) (A : Finset V) (hA : (N.cut A).card = 3)
    (ha : 2 ≤ A.card) (ho : 2 ≤ Aᶜ.card)
    (P : Finset (N.regionEdges A)) (Q : Finset (N.regionEdges Aᶜ))
    (hP : ∀ v, (((N.cap A).star v).filter (· ∈ P)).card = 1)
    (hQ : ∀ v, (((N.cap Aᶜ).star v).filter (· ∈ Q)).card = 1)
    (hPc : ((N.cap A).restrict (Subtype.val : ↥Pᶜ → N.regionEdges A)).graph.Connected)
    (hQc : ((N.cap Aᶜ).restrict (Subtype.val : ↥Qᶜ → N.regionEdges Aᶜ)).graph.Connected)
    (hcut : ∀ e ∈ N.cut A, e ∈ P.image Subtype.val ↔ e ∈ Q.image Subtype.val) :
    (N.restrict (Subtype.val : ↥(P.image Subtype.val ∪ Q.image Subtype.val)ᶜ → E)).graph.Connected
subject: Combinatorics
title: Gluing connected matching complements across a cut

question: For a nonempty finite set of paired triangular states and real corner weights, assume every permutation cycle has delta -3 with positive slope, or delta 3 with negative slope. Prove the sum of their polynomial terms is nonzero.
statement:
theorem total_sum_ne_zero (hex : Nonempty (@Pair A V T X)) (w : A → Fin 3 → ℝ)
    (hsign : ∀ (P : @Pair A V T X) c,
      (P.cycleDelta c = -3 ∧ 0 < P.cycleSlope w c) ∨
      (P.cycleDelta c = 3 ∧ P.cycleSlope w c < 0)) :
    (∑ P : @Pair A V T X, term w P) ≠ 0
subject: Combinatorics
title: Noncancellation of the paired-state polynomial

question: In the supplied primal-dual triangular-face network, let a state injectively assign each nonroot black vertex to an incident dual corner and cover exactly the corners outside the root face. For a dual cycle whose edge choices agree with the state, and a primal region A avoiding the root with that cycle as its cut, prove |black vertices in A| + |cut A| = |region dual vertices| + |black cut A|.
statement:
theorem state_disk_count (h : N.Duality D) (sD : D.Simple)
    (face : ∀ v, D.Triangle (N.star v)) (black : V → Prop)
    (hc : ∀ e, black (N.tail e) ↔ ¬black (N.head e)) (root : V)
    (m : V → F)
    (hm_inj : Set.InjOn m {v | black v ∧ v ≠ root})
    (hm_face : ∀ v, black v → v ≠ root → m v ∈ Set.range (face v).corner)
    (hm_range : ∀ z, z ∉ Set.range (face root).corner ↔
      ∃ v, black v ∧ v ≠ root ∧ m v = z)
    (C : Barnette.CycleCoordinates D.graph)
    (hchoice : ∀ i, N.blackEndpoint black (D.cycleEdge C i) ≠ root ∧
      m (N.blackEndpoint black (D.cycleEdge C i)) = C.vertex i)
    (A : Finset V) (hroot : root ∉ A) (hcut : N.cut A = D.cycleEdges C) :
    (A.filter black).card + (N.cut A).card =
      (N.regionVertices D A).card + (N.blackCut black A).card
subject: Combinatorics
title: A state-dependent disk counting identity

question: For the source’s prefix-plus-tail-extrema probes fProbe, assume I and Y differ from T only by small sets. Given j and ε>0, find a single finite block cutoff N≥j such that any intermediate sets I⊆X,Z⊆Y agreeing below N have |fProbe(T,n,X)−fProbe(T,n,Z)|<ε simultaneously for all n≤j.
statement:
lemma fProbe_block_continuity {T I Y : Set E0} (hI : SameClass T I) (hY : SameClass T Y)
    (j : ℕ) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ N, j ≤ N ∧ ∀ X Z, I ⊆ X → X ⊆ Y → I ⊆ Z → Z ⊆ Y →
      (∀ x, x.1.1 < N → (x ∈ X ↔ x ∈ Z)) →
      ∀ n ≤ j, |fProbe T n X - fProbe T n Z| < ε
subject: Combinatorics
title: Prove finite-block continuity despite infinite-tail probe terms

question: For a cylinder-continuous sequence of real set-probes on [I,Y], assume deleting one element lowers each probe by at most one and finite extensions of I have arbitrarily late negative probes. Starting from I⊆X⊆Y, construct a finite deletion Z preserving earlier probes within ε, attaining a nonpositive probe at some n≥j, and either leaving X unchanged or keeping every later probe ≥−1.
statement:
lemma deletion_stage
    {f : ℕ → Set ℕ → ℝ} {I Y X : Set ℕ}
    (hcc : CylinderContinuous f I Y)
    (hone : ∀ n A B, I ⊆ A → A ⊆ B → B ⊆ Y →
      (∃ e, B ⊆ insert e A) → f n B ≤ f n A + 1)
    (hlow : ∀ Z, I ⊆ Z → Z ⊆ Y → (Z \ I).Finite →
      ∀ j, ∃ n ≥ j, f n Z < 0)
    (hIX : I ⊆ X) (hXY : X ⊆ Y) (j : ℕ) (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ Z, I ⊆ Z ∧ Z ⊆ X ∧ (X \ Z).Finite ∧
      (∃ n ≥ j, f n Z ≤ 0) ∧
      (∀ n < j, |f n X - f n Z| < ε) ∧
      (Z = X ∨ ∀ n ≥ j, -1 ≤ f n Z)
subject: Combinatorics
title: One controlled finite deletion stage

question: Under the specified monotonicity, cylinder continuity, one-element Lipschitz bound, lower finite-extension negativity and eventual upper-endpoint positivity assumptions, construct I⊆Z⊆Y with arbitrarily late nonpositive probes and eventual lower bounds f_n(Z)≥−1−ε for every ε>0.
statement:
lemma infinite_endpoint_interpolation
    {f : ℕ → Set ℕ → ℝ} {I Y : Set ℕ} (hIY : I ⊆ Y)
    (hcc : CylinderContinuous f I Y)
    (hmono : ∀ n A B, I ⊆ A → A ⊆ B → B ⊆ Y → f n A ≤ f n B)
    (hone : ∀ n A B, I ⊆ A → A ⊆ B → B ⊆ Y →
      (∃ e, B ⊆ insert e A) → f n B ≤ f n A + 1)
    (hlow : ∀ Z, I ⊆ Z → Z ⊆ Y → (Z \ I).Finite →
      ∀ j, ∃ n ≥ j, f n Z < 0)
    (hhigh : ∃ j, ∀ n ≥ j, 0 < f n Y) :
    ∃ Z, I ⊆ Z ∧ Z ⊆ Y ∧
      (∀ j, ∃ n ≥ j, f n Z ≤ 0) ∧
      (∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ j, ∀ n ≥ j, -1 - ε ≤ f n Z)
subject: Combinatorics
title: Interpolate infinitely many endpoint probe constraints

question: For fewer than continuum many sets T_i, an interval A⊆Z satisfying the source rank-status assumptions, and nonsmall differences T_i\A and Z\T_i, construct an admissible B between A and Z such that both B\T_i and T_i\B remain nonsmall for every i.
statement:
lemma insert_prototype {ι : Type} (hι : Cardinal.mk ι < Cardinal.continuum)
    (T : ι → Set E0) {A Z : Set E0} (hAZ : A ⊆ Z)
    (hA : ¬ R.Upper A) (hZ : ¬ R.Lower Z)
    (hTA : ∀ i, ¬ Small (T i \ A)) (hZT : ∀ i, ¬ Small (Z \ T i)) :
    ∃ B, A ⊆ B ∧ B ⊆ Z ∧ R.Admissible B ∧
      ∀ i, ¬ Small (B \ T i) ∧ ¬ Small (T i \ B)
subject: Combinatorics
title: Insert a simultaneously separated admissible prototype

question: For the specified growing finite blocks, suppose G has block density at least δ at arbitrarily late blocks. Given positive b_j≤δ tending to zero and requested lower indices N_j, construct a small subset P⊆G whose density reaches at least b_j at some block m≥N_j for every j.
statement:
lemma exists_small_spikes {G : Set E0} {δ : ℝ} (_hδ : 0 < δ)
    (hG : ∀ N, ∃ m, N ≤ m ∧ δ ≤ density G m)
    (b : ℕ → ℝ) (hbpos : ∀ j, 0 < b j) (hble : ∀ j, b j ≤ δ)
    (hbzero : Tendsto b atTop (𝓝 0)) (N : ℕ → ℕ) :
    ∃ P : Set E0, P ⊆ G ∧ Small P ∧ ∀ j, ∃ m, N j ≤ m ∧ b j ≤ density P m
subject: Combinatorics
title: Construct a small set with prescribed density spikes

question: For the source’s block-probe construction, let X lie in the same small-symmetric-difference class as T and let G be a nonsmall subset of the complement of X. Construct a small P⊆G such that fProbe(T,n,X∪P) tends to +∞.
statement:
lemma positive_pool_add {T X G : Set E0} (hX : SameClass T X)
    (hG : ¬ Small G) (hGX : G ⊆ Xᶜ) :
    ∃ P, P ⊆ G ∧ Small P ∧ Tendsto (fun n ↦ fProbe T n (X ∪ P)) atTop atTop
subject: Combinatorics
title: Make probes diverge using a vanishing-density perturbation

question: Encode a finite multilinear form as a polynomial whose slots are assigned to variable blocks. If src occurs more often than dst and replacing any one src slot by dst makes the encoded polynomial zero, prove the original encoded polynomial is zero.
statement:
theorem multilinearPolynomial_eq_zero_of_replacements
    {V S I B : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    [Fintype S] [Fintype I] [Fintype B] [hS : DecidableEq S] [hB : DecidableEq B]
    (L : MultilinearMap ℂ (fun _ : S => V) ℂ) (e : I → V)
    (blocks : S → B) (src dst : B) (hsd : src ≠ dst)
    (hdegree : (Finset.univ.filter (fun s => blocks s = dst)).card <
      (Finset.univ.filter (fun s => blocks s = src)).card)
    (hzero : ∀ s, blocks s = src →
      multilinearPolynomial L e (Function.update blocks s dst) = 0) :
    multilinearPolynomial L e blocks = 0
subject: Algebra
title: Cancel all single-slot replacements

question: For finite-dimensional V and r(r+1)≤r+m, suppose the specified (r+1)-linear form vanishes whenever its first argument is t^(r+m) and each other argument is x^r·Q_i, for every x,t∈V and every Q_i∈Sym^m(V). Prove it vanishes on independently chosen pure (r+m)th powers in every argument.
statement:
theorem second_transfer [FiniteDimensional ℂ V] (r m : ℕ)
    (hb : r * (r+1) ≤ r+m)
    (T : SymmetricMultilinearForm (r+1) (r+m) V)
    (h : ∀ x t : V, ∀ Q : Fin r → SymPow m V,
      T (Fin.cons (symMonomial (r+m) V (fun _ => t))
        (fun i => symPowMul r m (symMonomial r V (fun _ => x)) (Q i))) = 0) :
    ∀ v : Fin (r+1) → V,
      T (fun i => symMonomial (r+m) V (fun _ => v i)) = 0
subject: Algebra
title: Remove a common power through the second transfer

question: For the supplied first-transfer labeling of an (r+1)×(r+m) slot grid at stage k<m, prove that shifting the remaining t block toward the kth target block differentiates its encoded flattened form to (r+m−k) times the encoding at stage k+1.
statement:
theorem firstLabel_derivative
    (r m k : ℕ) (hk : k < m) (V K : Type*)
    [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] [Fintype K]
    (T : SymmetricMultilinearForm (r+1) (r+m) V) (e : K → V)
    (D : Derivation ℂ (MvPolynomial (FirstBlock m × K) ℂ)
      (MvPolynomial (FirstBlock m × K) ℂ))
    (hD : ∀ q j, D (MvPolynomial.X (q,j)) =
      if q = some none then MvPolynomial.X (some (some ⟨k,hk⟩),j) else 0) :
    D (multilinearPolynomial (flattenedForm T) e
        (firstLabel r m k)) =
      ((r+m-k : ℕ) : ℂ) •
        multilinearPolynomial (flattenedForm T) e
          (firstLabel r m (k+1))
subject: Algebra
title: Compute the exact first-transfer derivative

question: Assume exactly the first-transfer, second-transfer and pure-power-extensionality principles in the supplied statement. Prove that for a,b≥1 with a(a−1)≤b, every symmetric a-linear form on Sym^b(V) vanishing on all repeated product inputs is zero.
statement:
theorem vanishing_induction_from_transfer_steps
    (firstTransfer : ∀ r m : ℕ, 0 < r → 0 < m → (r+1)*r ≤ r+m →
      ∀ T : SymmetricMultilinearForm (r+1) (r+m) V,
      IsSymmetricMultilinearForm (r+1) (r+m) V T →
      (∀ y : Fin (r+m) → V, T (fun _ => symMonomial (r+m) V y) = 0) →
      ∀ x t : V, ∀ y : Fin m → V,
        lowerProductForm r m T x t (fun _ => symMonomial m V y) = 0)
    (secondTransfer : ∀ r m : ℕ, 0 < r → 0 < m → (r+1)*r ≤ r+m →
      ∀ T : SymmetricMultilinearForm (r+1) (r+m) V,
      IsSymmetricMultilinearForm (r+1) (r+m) V T →
      (∀ x t : V, ∀ Q : Fin r → SymPow m V, lowerProductForm r m T x t Q = 0) →
      ∀ v : Fin (r+1) → V,
        T (fun i => symMonomial (r+m) V (fun _ => v i)) = 0)
    (purePowerExt : ∀ a b : ℕ, ∀ T : SymmetricMultilinearForm a b V,
      (∀ v : Fin a → V, T (fun i => symMonomial b V (fun _ => v i)) = 0) → T = 0) :
    ∀ a b : ℕ, 1 ≤ a → 1 ≤ b → a*(a-1) ≤ b →
      ∀ T : SymmetricMultilinearForm a b V,
      IsSymmetricMultilinearForm a b V T →
      (∀ y : Fin b → V, T (fun _ => symMonomial b V y) = 0) → T = 0
subject: Algebra
title: Assemble the two transfers into plethysm vanishing

question: For a positive-mass compatible grid entry satisfying the stated light-mass, light-entry, and clump-size hypotheses, show that the mean columnCost over random column order is at least 1−exposureError(A,D,H,K,i).
statement:
lemma average_columnCost_good {A D : ℕ} (hD : 2 ≤ D) (Q : Law (Grid A D))
    (a : Grid A D) (hQa : 0 < Q.mass a) (ha : Compatible a.1 a.2)
    {H K : ℝ} (hH : 0 ≤ H) (k : Fin D) (i : Fin A)
    (hL : 1/2 ≤ (columnPrediction Q k i (colHistory k i a)).prob
      (columnLight Q H k i (colHistory k i a)))
    (haL : columnLight Q H k i (colHistory k i a) (a.2 k i))
    (hK : (entryClumpSize k i a : ℝ) ≤ K) :
    1 - exposureError A D H K i ≤
      (Law.uniform : Law (Equiv.Perm (Fin D))).mean (fun e => columnCost Q H e k i a)
subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
title: Charge entropy to a light entry with a small clump

question: For uniform independent row permutations r and threshold H≥0, prove the displayed product bound on E exp(z·clumpCount(H,r)) in terms of the subset weight sum with factor (exp(1)/|β|)^|s|.
statement:
lemma clump_exp_moment_le {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    (H z : ℝ) (hH : 0 ≤ H) (hn : 0 < Fintype.card β) :
    uniformMean (fun r : α → Equiv.Perm β => Real.exp (z * clumpCount H r)) ≤
      (∑ s : Finset α, clumpWeight H z s *
        (Real.exp 1 / Fintype.card β) ^ s.card) ^ (Fintype.card β ^ 2)
subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
title: Bound the exponential moment of permutation clumps

question: For a law supported on compatible grids and H,K≥0, prove that AD minus totalExposureError, three times the total expected heavy-entry mass, and expected clumpCount is at most the sum of row/column marginal entropies minus joint entropy.
statement:
lemma grid_entropy_charge {A D : ℕ} (hD : 2 ≤ D) (Q : Law (Grid A D))
    (hQ : ∀ a, 0 < Q.mass a → Compatible a.1 a.2)
    {H K : ℝ} (hH : 0 ≤ H) (hK : 0 ≤ K) :
    (A : ℝ) * D - totalExposureError A D H K -
      3 * (∑ k : Fin D, ∑ i : Fin A, Q.mean (entryHeavyMass Q H k i)) -
      Q.mean (fun a => (clumpCount K a.1 : ℝ)) ≤
      (Q.map Prod.fst).entropy + (∑ k : Fin D, (Q.map (fun a => a.2 k)).entropy) - Q.entropy
subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
title: Aggregate entry costs into a grid entropy deficit

question: Given a finite law P, observables X,Y, positive-on-support predictor K(Y), and an always-satisfied support constraint S, prove the displayed bound on expected light-event log exclusion cost by prediction cross-entropy minus H(X|Y).
statement:
lemma condEntropy_light_comparison (P : Law α) (X : α → β) (Y : α → γ)
    (K : γ → Law β) (L S : γ → β → Prop)
    (hK : ∀ a, 0 < P.mass a → 0 < (K (Y a)).mass (X a))
    (hS : ∀ a, 0 < P.mass a → S (Y a) (X a)) :
    P.mean (fun a => if L (Y a) (X a) then
      -Real.log ((K (Y a)).prob (fun b => L (Y a) b ∧ S (Y a) b) /
        (K (Y a)).prob (L (Y a))) else 0) ≤
      -P.mean (fun a => Real.log ((K (Y a)).mass (X a))) - P.condEntropy X Y
subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
title: Relate light-event exclusion cost to prediction entropy

question: Let S(j,k) be specified subsets of row labels α, with finite β nonempty. For uniformly independent permutations r_i of β, prove P[∀j,k,i∈S(j,k), r_i(j)=k]≤(e/|β|)^(Σ_(j,k)|S(j,k)|).
statement:
lemma meetsLists_probability_le {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    (hn : 0 < Fintype.card β)
    (S : β × β → Finset α) :
    uniformProbability (MeetsLists S) ≤
      (Real.exp 1 / Fintype.card β) ^ (∑ b, (S b).card)
subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
title: Simultaneous incidence constraints on independent permutations

question: Let B be a finite law, f map its states to Fin D with D≥2, and let the fiber f=k have positive mass α. Prove that averaging −log B{b:e(k)≤e(f(b))} over uniform permutations e is at least 1−(1+log D)/D−α(1+log D).
statement:
lemma random_order_exclusion {β : Type*} [Fintype β] {D : ℕ} (hD : 2 ≤ D)
    (B : Law β) (f : β → Fin D) (k : Fin D)
    (hα : 0 < B.prob (fun b => f b = k)) :
    1 - (1 + Real.log (D : ℝ)) / (D : ℝ) -
        B.prob (fun b => f b = k) * (1 + Real.log (D : ℝ)) ≤
      (Law.uniform : Law (Equiv.Perm (Fin D))).mean
        (fun e => -Real.log (B.prob (fun b => e k ≤ e (f b))))
subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
title: Entropy cost of random-order exclusion

question: For a geometric action on the supplied CAT(0)-type metric structure and a sequence satisfying BraidRelations 39, prove 143·ℓ((s₀)²)² ≤57·ℓ((s₀s₁)³)², where ℓ is stableLengthAt at the chosen point.
statement:
lemma braid_forty_squared (hG : GeometricAction G X) (x : X)
    {s : ℕ → G} (hs : BraidRelations 39 s) :
    143 * stableLengthAt x ((s 0)^2)^2 ≤ 57 * stableLengthAt x ((s 0*s 1)^3)^2
subject: Group theory
title: Prove the 143-to-57 braid length obstruction

question: Under the exact mesh, patch, chart-error, displacement, mirror-error and inner/outer separation assumptions in the supplied statement, prove that the sum of ray-index occurrences over the selected refined faces is zero.
statement:
lemma refined_index_zero (hM : M.Exact) (hP : P.Exact)
    {C C₀ D w R : ℝ} (hw : D+1<w)
    (hchart : ∀ i p q, |dist (chart y i p•y) (chart y i q•y)-
      ‖vec (cosine y i) (q.1-p.1,q.2-p.2)‖|≤C)
    (hmetric : ∀ f p, dist (L.vertex (Replacement.vertex M P S (f,p))•y) (z (M.tail (f,0))•y)≤C₀)
    (hmirror : ∀ f p d, |mirrorVector (L.vertex (Replacement.vertex M P S (f,p))) d-
      mirrorVector (z (M.tail (f,0))) d|≤D)
    (hinner : ∀ f, Q f → ∃ i p, 0≤p.1 ∧ 0≤p.2 ∧ z (M.tail (f,0))=chart y i p)
    (houter : ∀ f, ¬Q f → R≤dist y (z (M.tail (f,0))•y))
    (hgap : (rayLength y 0+rayLength y 1)*(w+D+2)+C+2*C₀<R) :
    (∑ f : F × A, if Q f.1 then RayIndex.occurrence (Replacement.mesh M P S) L (mirrorAt w) f else 0) = 0
subject: Group theory
title: Force the localized refined ray index to vanish

question: For the explicitly defined capped cylindrical triangular grid patch of height H and circumference N>0, prove every real edge cochain antisymmetric across paired darts and summing to zero on each face is the difference of a vertex potential along every dart.
statement: theorem exact : (patch H N).Exact
subject: Group theory
title: Construct a potential for every cocycle on the explicit grid disk

question: Using the source’s explicit seam quotient and side-reversing gluing construction, prove that replacing every face of an exact triangular mesh M by an exact triangular patch P preserves exactness: every closed edge cochain on the replacement has a global vertex potential.
statement: theorem exact (hM : M.Exact) (hP : P.Exact) : (mesh M P S).Exact
subject: Group theory
title: Glue local potentials across the explicit patch-replacement seams

question: For a geometric action of TriangleGroup and any nonnegative edge bound B, choose subdivision constants before seeing a finite labeled triangular mesh. Prove every such mesh has a simplicial refinement with uniformly bounded metric and mirror-coordinate displacement and exactly preserved original corner labels, as quantified in the source statement.
statement:
theorem controlled_refinement (hG : GeometricAction TriangleGroup X) (y : X)
    (B : ℝ) (hB : 0≤B) :
    ∃ K H : ℕ, ∃ hK : 0<K, letI : NeZero K := ⟨by omega⟩;
      ∃ C D : ℝ, 0≤C ∧ 0≤D ∧
      ∀ (F V : Type) [Fintype F] (M : TriangleMesh F V) (z : V → TriangleGroup),
      (∀ f i, dist (z (M.tail (f,i))•y) (z (M.tail (f,i+1))•y) ≤ B) →
      ∃ L : (Replacement.mesh M (GridDisk.patch H (3*K)) (GridDisk.sides H K)).SimplicialLabeling,
        (∀ f p,
          dist (L.vertex (Replacement.vertex M (GridDisk.patch H (3*K)) (GridDisk.sides H K) (f,p)) • y)
            (z (M.tail (f,0))•y) ≤ C) ∧
        (∀ f p d,
          |mirrorVector (L.vertex (Replacement.vertex M (GridDisk.patch H (3*K)) (GridDisk.sides H K) (f,p))) d-
            mirrorVector (z (M.tail (f,0))) d| ≤ D) ∧
        (∀ f i, L.vertex (Replacement.vertex M (GridDisk.patch H (3*K)) (GridDisk.sides H K)
            (f,(GridDisk.sides H K).point (i,0))) = z (M.tail (f,i)))
subject: Group theory
title: Uniformly refine every bounded-edge triangular mesh

question: Let commuting g,h have positive stable lengths and normalized length pairing c with |c|≤1. For the prescribed floor-rounded lattice map from R² to G, prove a single additive constant bounds the discrepancy between orbit distance and the c-dependent Euclidean norm for every pair of real points.
statement:
theorem lattice_metric (hG : GeometricAction G X) (y : X) {g h : G}
    (hg : 0<stableLengthAt y g) (hh : 0<stableLengthAt y h) (hcomm : Commute g h)
    {c : ℝ} (hc : |c|≤1)
    (hp : lengthPairing y g h = c*stableLengthAt y g*stableLengthAt y h) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 ≤ C ∧ ∀ p q : Point,
      |dist (lattice g h (stableLengthAt y g) (stableLengthAt y h) p • y)
          (lattice g h (stableLengthAt y g) (stableLengthAt y h) q • y) -
        ‖vec c (q.1-p.1,q.2-p.2)‖| ≤ C
subject: Group theory
title: Bound the metric error of a rounded flat lattice

question: If 0<a<b and (a+b)/2<u, show that for all sufficiently large natural N there exists a polynomial with degree ≤N^u, weight_N≤exp(N^u), value 1 at zero, and magnitude ≤exp(−N^a) on integers 1 through ceil(N^b).
statement:
theorem polynomial_approximation {a b u : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (hab : a < b)
    (hu : (a + b) / 2 < u) :
    ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop, ∃ p : ℝ[X],
      (p.natDegree : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) ^ u ∧ weight N p ≤ Real.exp ((N : ℝ) ^ u) ∧
      p.eval 0 = 1 ∧ ∀ x : ℕ, 1 ≤ x → x ≤ ⌈(N : ℝ) ^ b⌉₊ →
        |p.eval (x : ℝ)| ≤ Real.exp (-((N : ℝ) ^ a))
subject: Mathematical physics
title: Choose asymptotic parameters for a low-cost spectral filter

question: For the projectors, unitary, polynomial, and four norm estimates in the exact statement, prove ||M.high(r)·conjugate(U,D.zero)·M.zero||² ≤ A+E+(1+B)T.
statement:
lemma Count.backward_finite {N : ℕ} (M D : Count N) (U : Operator N) (hU : U ∈ unitary (Operator N))

subject: Mathematical physics
title: Convert polynomial approximation into a squared transition bound

question: For arbitrary product-projection counts M,D on N qubits and real threshold r, prove ||M.high(r)·D.zero·M.zero||²≤2^(−r). No disjointness hypothesis on M and D is available.
statement:
lemma Count.depth_zero_square {N : ℕ} (M D : Count N) (r : ℝ) :

question: Assume all depth-d localization estimates and one depth-(d+1) estimate at scales (t,b). Under 0≤s<a<u<w<t<b and (a+b)/2<u, prove UniformLocalization(d+1,s,t).
statement:
