question: For a unitary circuit on N≥n>0 qubits with initially zero ancillas, suppose its designated output predicts every input parity with success at least 1/2+ε. If every displayed Hadamard-conjugated complement entry of the output-zero projector has norm at most δ, prove ε≤δ.
statement:
lemma parity_advantage_from_entries {n N : ℕ} (hn : 0<n) (hnN : n ≤ N)
    (W : Operator N) (hW : W ∈ unitary (Operator N)) (out : Fin N) {ε δ : ℝ}
    (hsuccess : ∀ x : Word n, 1/2+ε ≤ successProbability W out x)
    (hentry : ∀ x : Word n,
      ‖(localMatrix (inputHadamard n N)*(star W*(outputZeroCount out).zero*W)*
        localMatrix (inputHadamard n N)) (flipWord (inputSet n N) (inputWord x)) (inputWord x)‖ ≤ δ) :
    ε ≤ δ
subject: Mathematical physics
title: Recover parity advantage from ancilla-aware off-diagonal entries

question: For the source polynomial approxPoly(r,m,k), prove simultaneously the stated degree bound, weighted coefficient bound, value 1 at zero, and exponentially small values at every integer 1≤x≤m under the displayed Chebyshev-size condition.
statement:
lemma approxPoly_bounds {r m k : ℕ} {R : ℝ} (hR : 0 ≤ R)
    (hr : 1 ≤ r) (hm : 2 * r ≤ m)
    (hk : 4 * (r : ℝ) * Real.log m ≤ (k : ℝ) * Real.sqrt ((r : ℝ) / m)) :
    (approxPoly r m k).natDegree ≤ r + k ∧
    weight R (approxPoly r m k) ≤ (1 + R) ^ r * (7 + 4 * R) ^ k ∧
    (approxPoly r m k).eval 0 = 1 ∧
    ∀ x : ℕ, 1 ≤ x → x ≤ m →
      |(approxPoly r m k).eval (x : ℝ)| ≤ 2 * Real.exp (-(3 * (r : ℝ) * Real.log m))
subject: Mathematical physics
title: Degree, coefficient cost, and decay of the QAC filter polynomial

question: Given the three successive transition estimates h₁,h₂,h₃ in the exact statement, prove the norm bound 9^|supp(A)|·3δ after conjugating A.zero by a unitary V, a disjoint reflection layer R, and a local layer L.
statement:
lemma small_support_layer_bound {N : ℕ} (V : Operator N) (hV : V ∈ unitary (Operator N))
    (R : ReflectionLayer N) (L : LocalLayer N) (M A : Count N) {r r₁ r₂ δ : ℝ} (hδ : 0 ≤ δ)
    (h₁ : ∀ D : Count N, ‖M.high r₁*conjugate V D.zero*M.zero‖ ≤ δ)
    (h₂ : ∀ D : Count N, ‖M.high r₂*conjugate V D.zero*M.low r₁‖ ≤ δ)
    (h₃ : ∀ D : Count N, ‖M.high r*conjugate V D.zero*M.low r₂‖ ≤ δ) :
    ‖M.high r*conjugate (V*reflectionMatrix R*localMatrix L) A.zero*M.zero‖ ≤
      (9:ℝ)^A.support.card*(3*δ)
subject: Mathematical physics
title: Propagate a small-support projector through a reflection layer

question: For n,m>0 let K={z:expLevel(v,b,z)≤1} be compact and contain the numerical range of A strictly in its interior. If a matrix polynomial F has norm≤1 throughout K, prove ||tensorPolynomial A F||≤2, using the pinned numerical-range and tensor-polynomial definitions.
statement:
theorem expLevel_domain_bound {n m : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hm : 0 < m)
    (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ) {ι : Type u_144} [Fintype ι]
    (v : ι → ℂ) (b : ι → ℝ) (hc : IsCompact {z | Geometry.expLevel v b z ≤ 1})
    (hW : ∀ z ∈ numericalRange A, Geometry.expLevel v b z < 1)
    (F : MatrixPolynomial m)
    (hF : ∀ z, Geometry.expLevel v b z ≤ 1 → ‖matrixPolynomialValue z F‖ ≤ 1) :
    ‖tensorPolynomial A F‖ ≤ 2
subject: Functional analysis
title: Transfer a convex exponential domain to a matrix polynomial bound

question: Let n,m>0. Given the exact Faber-type basis expansion and two-sided energy hypotheses, a continuous R whose negative Fourier coefficients are b_k(A), no positive Fourier modes, and R(t)+R(t)* positive semidefinite, prove that any matrix polynomial F of boundary norm at most 1 satisfies ||tensorPolynomial A F||≤2. Retain every hypothesis in the Lean statement.
statement:
theorem analytic_domain_core {n m : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hm : 0 < m)
    (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ) (b : ℕ → Polynomial ℂ) (hb0 : b 0 = 1)
    (h : BoundaryCircle → ℂ) (hh : Continuous h)
    (hexpand : ∀ G : MatrixPolynomial m, ∃ (N : ℕ) (C : Fin N → Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) ℂ),
      G = faberPolynomial b C)
    (hlower : ∀ N (C : Fin N → Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) ℂ),
      ∑ k, hsSq (C k) ≤ polynomialEnergy h (faberPolynomial b C))
    (hupper : ∀ N (C : Fin N → Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) ℂ),
      polynomialEnergy h (faberPolynomial b C) ≤ ∑ k : Fin N, faberWeight k * hsSq (C k))
    (R : BoundaryCircle → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ) (hR : Continuous R)
    (hcoeff : ∀ k : ℕ, fourierCoeff R (-(k : ℤ)) = Polynomial.aeval A (b k))
    (hposfreq : ∀ k : ℤ, 0 < k → fourierCoeff R k = 0)
    (hpositive : ∀ t, (R t + (R t)ᴴ).PosSemidef)
    (F : MatrixPolynomial m) (hF : ∀ t, ‖matrixPolynomialValue (h t) F‖ ≤ 1) :
    ‖tensorPolynomial A F‖ ≤ 2
subject: Functional analysis
title: Derive the factor-two matrix norm bound from boundary data

question: For the pinned exponential level function expLevel(v,b), assume a strict interior point a, ψ differentiable with nonzero derivative at |ζ|=1, ψ maps the unit circle to level 1, and ψ maps |η|≥1 outside that sublevel. For every w with expLevel(v,b,w)≤1, prove ⟨ζ ψ′(ζ),ψ(ζ)−w⟩_R≥0.
statement:
theorem expLevel_holomorphic_support {ι : Type u_143} [Fintype ι]
    (v : ι → ℂ) (b : ι → ℝ) {a : ℂ} (ha : expLevel v b a < 1)
    {ψ : ℂ → ℂ} {ζ : ℂ} (hζ : ‖ζ‖ = 1)
    (hd : HasDerivAt ψ (deriv ψ ζ) ζ) (hdn : deriv ψ ζ ≠ 0)
    (hcircle : ∀ η : ℂ, ‖η‖ = 1 → expLevel v b (ψ η) = 1)
    (hout : ∀ η : ℂ, 1 ≤ ‖η‖ → 1 ≤ expLevel v b (ψ η))
    {w : ℂ} (hw : expLevel v b w ≤ 1) :
    0 ≤ inner ℝ (ζ*deriv ψ ζ) (ψ ζ-w)
subject: Functional analysis
title: Recover a supporting normal from an exterior holomorphic map

question: For the pinned exterior map data c,g analytic on a disk of radius R>1, with nonzero c, nonvanishing chord denominators, and nonnegative boundary kernel, prove for every finite Hilbert-space coefficient family C that its squared coefficient norm sum is at most the angular boundary energy of its Faber series, and that this energy is at most the sum with weight 1 on k=0 and weight 2 on k>0.
statement:
theorem faber_hilbert_coefficient_bounds {R : ℝ} (hR : 1 < R) {g : ℂ → ℂ}
    (hg : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ g (ball 0 R)) {c : ℂ} (hc : c ≠ 0)
    (hH : ∀ u ∈ ball 0 R, ∀ v ∈ ball 0 R, chordDenominator c g u v ≠ 0)
    (hpositive : ∀ t s, 0 ≤ boundaryKernel c g t s)
    {N : ℕ} (C : Fin N → E) :
    (∑ k, ‖C k‖^2 ≤ ∫ t, ‖faberBoundarySeries c g C t‖^2 ∂angularMeasure) ∧
      ((∫ t, ‖faberBoundarySeries c g C t‖^2 ∂angularMeasure) ≤
        ∑ k : Fin N, (if (k:ℕ) = 0 then 1 else 2)*‖C k‖^2)
subject: Functional analysis
title: Two-sided Hilbert energy bounds for Faber coefficients

question: Assume a polynomial basis b supplies the stated lower and upper boundary-energy bounds and a continuous matrix resolvent R has negative Fourier coefficients b_k(A). For a boundary-contracting matrix polynomial F and singular pair X,Y with singular value γ>0, prove both weighted diagonal coefficient-energy series are bounded by γ⁻² times the cross energy integral of Y*R X. The exact statement specifies the weight 1/2 on positive indices.
statement:
theorem singular_diagonal_estimates {n m : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ)
    (b : ℕ → Polynomial ℂ) (h : BoundaryCircle → ℂ) (hh : Continuous h)
    (hexpand : ∀ G : MatrixPolynomial m, ∃ (N : ℕ) (C : Fin N → Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) ℂ),
      G = faberPolynomial b C)
    (hlower : ∀ N (C : Fin N → Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) ℂ),
      ∑ k, hsSq (C k) ≤ polynomialEnergy h (faberPolynomial b C))
    (hupper : ∀ N (C : Fin N → Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) ℂ),
      polynomialEnergy h (faberPolynomial b C) ≤ ∑ k : Fin N, faberWeight k * hsSq (C k))
    (R : BoundaryCircle → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ) (hR : Continuous R)
    (hcoeff : ∀ k : ℕ, fourierCoeff R (-(k : ℤ)) = Polynomial.aeval A (b k))
    (F : MatrixPolynomial m) (hF : ∀ t, ‖matrixPolynomialValue (h t) F‖ ≤ 1)
    (X Y : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin m) ℂ) (γ : ℝ) (hγ : 0 < γ)
    (hFx : Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (n := Fin n × Fin m) (𝕜 := ℂ) (tensorPolynomial A F) (hsVector X) =
      (γ : ℂ) • hsVector Y)
    (hFy : ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint
      (Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (n := Fin n × Fin m) (𝕜 := ℂ) (tensorPolynomial A F)) (hsVector Y) =
      (γ : ℂ) • hsVector X) :
    let a := ∫ t, hsSq (Yᴴ * R t * X) ∂circleMeasure
    (hsSq (Xᴴ * Polynomial.aeval A (b 0) * X) + (1/2 : ℝ) *
      ∑' k : ℕ, hsSq (Xᴴ * Polynomial.aeval A (b (k+1)) * X) ≤ a / γ^2) ∧
    (hsSq (Yᴴ * Polynomial.aeval A (b 0) * Y) + (1/2 : ℝ) *
      ∑' k : ℕ, hsSq (Yᴴ * Polynomial.aeval A (b (k+1)) * Y) ≤ a / γ^2)
subject: Functional analysis
title: Diagonal coefficient energy from a singular vector pair

question: For the pinned block at p≥1 with positive attachment radius, prove there is no operator T on its Lipschitz-free space with ||T||≤2p, range fixed by the finite-support projection onto S containing the base, and error<1 on every anchor. Preserve the graph, label, radius and block parameter definitions exactly.
statement:
theorem finite_support_impossible (hp : 1 ≤ p) (S : Finset (Block p)) (ho : base p ∈ S)
    (T : FreeSpace (base p) →L[ℝ] FreeSpace (base p))
    (hn : ‖T‖ ≤ 2*(p : ℝ))
    (hfixed : ∀ u, supportProjection (base p) (separation p) S (T u) = T u)
    (he : ∀ a ∈ anchors p, ‖T (delta (base p) a) - delta (base p) a‖ < 1) : False
subject: Functional analysis
title: Rule out bounded finite-support approximation on the metric block

question: In the pinned all-colorings graph over Cayley(A,N), with n≤N, suppose each state permits at most H colors and at most Q successors, and compatibility forces the current color into the permitted set. Prove the exact cardinal bound on roots failing Good: badRoots·|C|^(n+1)≤|A×Bool|^n·(|S|Q^n)·H^(n+1)·allRoots.
statement:
theorem rare_matched_bound (n N Q H : ℕ) (hnN : n ≤ N)
    (compatible : ((Cayley A N → C) × Cayley A N) → S → Prop)
    (trans : S → S → Prop) (P : S → Finset C)
    (hP : ∀ j, (P j).card ≤ H)
    (hcolor : ∀ z j, compatible z j → z.1 z.2 ∈ P j)
    (hQ : ∀ j, Fintype.card {k : S // trans j k} ≤ Q) :
    Nat.card {z : (Cayley A N → C) × Cayley A N //
        ¬ (allColoringsGraph A C N).Good compatible trans n z} * Nat.card C ^ (n+1) ≤
      Nat.card (A × Bool) ^ n * (Nat.card S * Q ^ n) * H ^ (n+1) *
        Nat.card ((Cayley A N → C) × Cayley A N)
subject: Functional analysis
title: Count roots admitting long compatible matched walks

question: For the pinned all-colorings sequence graph, assume the color count exceeds 2|A×Bool|QH, Q,H and degree are positive, each state has ≤H colors and ≤Q successors, and compatibility respects its allowed colors. For any V∈N find n≥2 such that 20V times the number of vertices not Good at depth n is strictly smaller than the number of vertices in that component.
statement:
theorem exists_rare_component (Q H V : ℕ) (hQpos : 0 < Q) (hHpos : 0 < H)
    (hDpos : 0 < Nat.card (A × Bool))
    (hk : 2 * Nat.card (A × Bool) * Q * H < Nat.card C)
    (compatible : Vertex A C → S → Prop) (trans : S → S → Prop) (P : S → Finset C)
    (hP : ∀ j, (P j).card ≤ H)
    (hcolor : ∀ z j, compatible z j → sequenceColor A C z ∈ P j)
    (hQ : ∀ j, Fintype.card {k : S // trans j k} ≤ Q) :
    ∃ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n ∧
      20 * V * Nat.card {z : (Cayley A n → C) × Cayley A n //
        ¬ (sequenceGraph A C).Good compatible trans n (intoSequence A C n z)} <
      Nat.card ((Cayley A n → C) × Cayley A n)
subject: Functional analysis
title: Find a sequence component with arbitrarily small bad-vertex density

question: In the separated pointed metric space of the exact statement, let T be supported on finite S, ||T||≤2p, and suppose an anchor a shares x’s label, dist(x,a)≤R and ||Tδ_a−δ_a||<1. For a 1-Lipschitz label map and L≥0,K>0,p≥0, prove that the affine weights of Tδ_x pair with the radius-K label bump by at least L−(L/K)(2pR+1).
statement:
theorem affine_bump_mass (o : M)
    (sep : ∀ x y : M, x ≠ y → 1 ≤ dist x y) (S : Finset M) (ho : o ∈ S)
    (T : FreeSpace o →L[ℝ] FreeSpace o)
    (hfixed : ∀ u, supportProjection o sep S (T u) = T u)
    (h : M → N) (hh : LipschitzWith 1 h) (x a : M) (ha : h a = h x)
    (L K p R : ℝ) (hL : 0 ≤ L) (hK : 0 < K) (hp : 0 ≤ p)
    (hn : ‖T‖ ≤ 2*p) (hR : dist x a ≤ R) (he : ‖T (delta o a) - delta o a‖ < 1) :
    L - (L/K)*(2*p*R+1) ≤
      pairing (affineWeights o sep S ho (T (delta o x)))
        (fun j : S => labelBump h (h x) L K j.val)
subject: Functional analysis
title: Force affine mass into a label bump

question: For the pinned metric-block construction with R>0 and 0<L≤K, every finite S, record depth n, vertex x and port e, construct a real 1-Lipschitz function f bounded by L. Outside the exception set at (x,e), it must equal the label bump centered at x; outside the exception set at the reversed endpoint (G.move x e,G.reverse e), it must equal the negative bump centered there. Keep the exact exceptionSet and label definitions.
statement:
theorem edge_test (hL : 0 < L) (hK : 0 < K) (hLK : L ≤ K)
    (S : Finset (Point G color cap R)) (n : ℕ) (x : X) (e : E) :
    ∃ f : Point G color cap R → ℝ, LipschitzWith 1 f ∧ (∀ z, |f z| ≤ L) ∧
      (∀ j : S, j ∉ exceptionSet G color cap R L K S n x e →
        f j.val = labelBump (label G color cap R) (originalLabel G color cap x) L K j.val) ∧
      (∀ j : S, j ∉ exceptionSet G color cap R L K S n (G.move x e) (G.reverse e) →
        f j.val = -labelBump (label G color cap R) (originalLabel G color cap (G.move x e)) L K j.val)
subject: Functional analysis
title: Build opposing Lipschitz tests across a graph edge

question: For finite nonempty vertex and port types X,D, signed measures μ_x on finite S with total variation≤V, and exceptional sets E_x,e disjoint across ports at good vertices, assume 20V<|D| and 20V·|bad|<|X|. Given an incidence-reversal bijection and the stated lower bound 15p−20p(error(e)+error(rev e))≤2p on every incidence, prove False for p>0.
statement:
theorem signed_incidence_obstruction [Nonempty X] [Nonempty D]
    (μ : X → S → ℝ) (E : X → D → Set S) (bad : Finset X)
    (rev : (X × D) ≃ (X × D)) (p V : ℝ)
    (hp : 0 < p) (hV : 0 ≤ V)
    (hTV : ∀ x, totalVariation (μ x) ≤ V)
    (hgood : ∀ x, x ∉ bad → ∀ j e f, j ∈ E x e → j ∈ E x f → e = f)
    (hdegree : 20 * V < (Fintype.card D : ℝ))
    (hbad : 20 * V * (bad.card : ℝ) < (Fintype.card X : ℝ))
    (hedge : ∀ e : X × D,
      3 * (10 * p) / 2 - 2 * (10 * p) *
        (variationOn (μ e.1) (E e.1 e.2) +
         variationOn (μ (rev e).1) (E (rev e).1 (rev e).2)) ≤ 2 * p) : False
subject: Functional analysis
title: Contradict edge constraints by signed incidence averaging
